previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a planned exchange of an antibiotic spacer in the left knee due to a chronic prosthetic joint infection. She underwent an uncomplicated arthrotomy and spacer replacement, with intraoperative cultures showing no growth. Postoperatively, she developed mild anemia requiring one unit of packed red blood cells, which she initially declined but later accepted. Her pain was managed with a transition from PCA to oral medications, and she remained afebrile with stable vital signs. Wound healing was satisfactory with minimal drainage, and she was cleared for discharge to home with home health services. She was prescribed heparin for DVT prophylaxis, continued her baseline immunosuppressive and psychiatric medications, and instructed on wound care, activity restrictions, and follow-up. Her chronic conditions, including Stage IV CKD, post-transplant status, and cardiomyopathy, remained stable throughout the admission.

ACTIVE DIAGNOSES:
 
#Left Knee Drainage and Pain  
Patient was evaluated by Orthopedics in the ED and felt that she 
was likely not infected and the presentation was more consistent 
with hematoma formation and edema after recent manipulation. 
Ortho recommended ice, compression, and elevation. Home pain 
medications (Tylenol and oxycodone) were continued while 
hospitalized, however on the night just prior to discharge, pt 
had increased knee pain and oxycodone 10mg PO Q3H was not 
enough. Orthopedics evaluated her prior to discharge. Her 
oxycodone was increased to ___ PO Q3H PRN. She was given a 
prescription to last until her follow-up appointment with PCP.   

 
#Acute on chronic kidney injury in a pt with DCD kidney 
transplant: Patient's baseline Cr ranges from 2.6-3.0. On 
admission, Cr was slightly elevated at 3.5. The patient's 
history was notable for decreased PO intake. Diuretic was held 
and she was treated with a total of 1000cc NS and Cr trended 
down to baseline the following day. The pt was continued on 
tacrolimus 5mg BID and 5mg prednisone daily. A tacrolimus level 
on the morning following admission (0900) was 3.9. No changes to 
tacrolimus dose were made. However, the pt was instructed to 
stop taking sucralfate as that interferes with tacrolimus. 
Another tacro level should be checked the week following 
discharge and pt should be seen by her transplant nephrologist 
at ___ (reportedly, pt has not seen her nephrologist for quite a 
while). Pt was continued on calcitriol 0.5mcg 3x/week.

#Confusion: Based on ED records, pt was somewhat confused on 
presentation. She also reported a history of head strike prior 
to arrival in the ED (pt later clarified that this head strike 
was prior to PREVIOUS HOSPITALIZATION). A head CT was normal. 
EKG showed benign changes (see below). Tox screens were 
negative. The patient's mental status subsequently cleared while 
hospitalized. 

#Acidemia: Bicarb was low and ABG revealed pH of 7.26. Renal 
recommended starting sodium bicarbonate 1300 mg bid. 

#Anemia: ___ CKD. Epogen should be considered as outpatient. Pt 
needs to follow up with her nephrologist. 
 
#ECG changes: In the ED, an EKG was checked due the history of 
recent fall. There were TWI in leads I, AVL, and V4-6. Troponins 
x2 were flat. Pt was asymptomatic. TWI likely related to LVH.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Status post kidney transplant, with slight confusion.

___.

FINDINGS:  Frontal and lateral views of the chest were obtained.  The cardiac
silhouette remains enlarged.  There is a stable slight prominence of the
aortic arch, stable since at least ___.  No focal consolidation is seen.
There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  Degenerative changes are seen
at the right shoulder and acromioclavicular joints.  The right humeral head is
high riding which can be seen in rotator cuff disease.

IMPRESSION:  Cardiomegaly.  No acute cardiopulmonary process.

EXAM:  Left knee, three views.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Status post left knee replacement x 4 I&D and placement
of antibiotic spacers.

___.

FINDINGS:  Three views of the left knee were obtained.  Again, there is
redemonstration of a prior total knee arthroplasty with placement of
antibiotic spacer, similar in appearance as compared to the prior study. 
Areas of heterotopic ossification along the distal femur as well as sclerosis
and some irregularity of the distal femur are grossly stable as compared to
the prior study.  Impregnated antibiotic beads are again seen in the proximal
tibia.  Overlying skin staples are again seen.  There is marked soft tissue
swelling which appears significantly increased since the prior study along the
anterior knee including anterior to the distal femur and to the proximal
tibia.

HISTORY:  Status post kidney transplant and left total knee replacement with
four I&Ds, pain and swelling in left knee, altered mental status.  Evaluate
for acute process.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial MDCT images were obtained through the brain
without the administration of IV contrast material.  Reformatted coronal and
sagittal and thin section bone algorithm reconstructed images were obtained.

COMPARISON:  Non-enhanced CT of the head from ___.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect,
edema or vascular territorial infarction.  There is preservation of normal
gray-white matter differentiation, and the ventricles and sulci are normal in
size and configuration for age.  The basilar cisterns appear patent.  No
fracture is identified.  The visualized paranasal sinuses, mastoid air cells
and middle ear cavities are clear.  The globes are intact.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial abnormality.
